Android adaptive icon — the two layers

You asked what I meant by “the empty foreground layer.” Every image on this page is your actual shipped asset, read straight from assets/images/. Nothing here is a drawing of the problem — it is the problem.

1 · How Android icons work

iOS takes one flat square. Android does not. It takes two layers, each 108×108dp, and every phone maker applies its own mask on top — circle on Pixel, squircle on Samsung, rounded square on OnePlus. The layers also move independently when you touch the icon (that little parallax wobble).

Backgroundcolour / gradient only
+
Foregroundthe mark, on transparency
→
OEM maskapplied by the phone
The rule that matters: the canvas is 108×108dp but only the centre 72×72dp is guaranteed visible, and the safe circle is 66×66dp — 61% of the width. Anything outside that gets eaten by somebody’s mask. The outer ring exists purely so the parallax has room to slide.

2 · What Whenbee ships today

Your app.json points at both layers. One of them is blank.

android-icon-background.pngwhole bee baked in here
+
100% transparent
alpha bbox = None
android-icon-foreground.pngcompletely empty
→
Resultbackground zoomed & cropped

The bee is sitting in the background layer. Android treats that layer as wallpaper — it scales it up to fill the 108dp canvas and then the mask cuts it. So instead of a bee inside a safe circle, you get a zoomed crop of a bee, and the two things that say bee — the antennae and the stripes — are the first to go.

Honest caveat on the right-hand mock: I built that foreground by colour-keying the bee out of your existing background PNG. The source art is already cropped at the abdomen, so the bottom edge is a flat cut. It proves the geometry, not the final art — the real fix needs the bee redrawn whole with margin, not a rescued cutout.
